title: Securing API routes with JWT and Auth0 during a CodeDay Labs internship
situation: During my CodeDay Labs software developer internship, I joined an existing MERN (MongoDB, Express, React, Node.js) application whose REST API was consumed by the UI. Some routes that changed data had no protection [confirm: the app's purpose].
task: Extend the REST API's functionality and protect its sensitive routes, while getting up to speed on an unfamiliar codebase within a short internship.
action: I traced how the React UI called the API to learn the codebase, then extended the Express endpoints the UI needed. For security, I integrated Auth0 and added JSON Web Token verification as Express middleware on the protected routes, so requests without a valid token were rejected before reaching the handlers. Public read routes stayed open. I coordinated with the team through GitHub pull requests and Notion.
result: The protected routes required a valid Auth0-issued JWT, and the API supported the new UI features [confirm: features shipped]. What I learned: how to become productive quickly in someone else's codebase, starting from how it's used, plus a lasting habit of treating authentication as middleware rather than per-route code.
